issues.title: Float fast-path exact-length checks no longer exercised by any too-long-payload test
issues.verdictReason: The pre-existing wrong_data_len tests (marshal_vector_test.go:369-386) send 10 bytes for a 3-dimension vector; the new bound at marshal.go:998-1003 (len(data)/elemMin < Dimensions) now rejects that before reaching the fast-path's own len(data)!=expected check at marshal.go:1012/1023, so only too-long payloads would still exercise those lines and no such test exists.
issues.scopeReason: The new bound this PR adds is what shadows the existing test and removes its coverage of the fast-path check.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Fast-path exact-length checks for *[]float64/*[]float32 now untested

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: The fast-path exact-length checks at marshal.go:1012 and marshal.go:1023 are now covered only by accident: existing wrong_data_len tests send too-short payloads that the new bound rejects first, so no test exercises these checks on too-long payloads; if the checks were loosened, extra bytes would be silently accepted.

issues.title: Empty non-NULL payload with dimensions > 0 now errors, change is untested
issues.verdictReason: Verified pre-PR behavior: for data=[]byte{} (non-nil) with Dimensions>0 and a fixed-size element, the old generic path computed elemSize=len(data)/Dimensions=0 and decoded zero values rather than erroring; the new bound at marshal.go:998-1003 now rejects this case. The only existing empty-payload test, TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType (marshal_vector_test.go:936-954), uses VectorType{} i.e. Dimensions=0, not >0, so this behavior change is untested.
issues.scopeReason: The behavior change is a direct, intended effect of this PR's new bound and has no covering test.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Empty non-NULL payload with dimensions > 0 erroring is an untested behavior change

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: The PR-declared behavior change where an empty non-NULL payload with dimensions above 0 now errors (marshal.go:998) has no test; every short-payload case uses 2 bytes and every []byte{} case uses dimension 0 (marshal_vector_test.go:641), so reverting the guard from len(data) > 0 to data != nil would silently reintroduce zero-value decoding without any test failing.

issues.title: vectorElemMinSize recomputes isVectorVariableLengthType at every recursion level,…
issues.verdictReason: vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1125) calls isVectorVariableLengthType(elemType) (line 1130), which itself recurses through all remaining nested-vector levels, then recurses into vectorElemMinSize(vec.SubType) (line 1135) one level down, repeating the full isVectorVariableLengthType walk there too; a microbenchmark against synthetic nested VectorTypes (depth 100/200/400/800) showed call cost growing much faster than linearly, confirming the quadratic claim. Nested vector types are a real feature (helpers.go asVectorType recurses with no depth cap), so this is reachable from a crafted or malicious schema, though only a CPU-burn concern, not a crash.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize is new code added by this PR; the quadratic behavior did not exist before it.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: vectorElemMinSize recomputes isVectorVariableLengthType recursively, causing quadratic complexity

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1130, marshal.go:1135) calls the recursive isVectorVariableLengthType at every level of its own recursion, making decode cost depth² instead of depth for deeply nested vector types, repeated per inner element; a malicious peer could use this to burn CPU, though it cannot crash the driver.

issues.title: New top-of-function comment wrongly claims every path allocates, but the array path does…
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed in the generic path (marshal.go:1078-1081): when k == reflect.Array, the code only validates rv.Len() against Dimensions and indexes into the caller-provided array; there is no make/reflect.MakeSlice call, contradicting the comment's claim that 'every path below turns it into an allocation'.
issues.scopeReason: The inaccurate comment is new text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: New comment incorrectly claims every path below allocates

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: The new comment at marshal.go:986 says "every path below turns it into an allocation," but the array path allocates nothing and instead computes element size as len(data)/Dimensions, decoding a short payload as zeros; a reader trusting the comment could wrongly exempt the array path from the new bound.

issues.title: Pre-existing comment about empty/dim=0 falling through to the generic path is now stale
issues.verdictReason: The comment at marshal.go:1006 predates this PR but is now inaccurate: the new bound added just above it (marshal.go:998-1003) intercepts an empty non-nil payload with Dimensions>0 and returns an error before any fall-through to the generic path occurs, which the comment no longer reflects.
issues.scopeReason: The comment was accurate before this PR; this PR's new bound is what made it stale.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Stale comment about nil/empty and dim=0 falling through to the generic path

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: The unchanged comment at marshal.go:1006 stating "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path" is now stale, since the new bound rejects an empty non-nil payload with dimensions above 0 before reaching that point.

issues.title: Claimed contradiction between commit message wording and the recursive minimum-size logic
issues.verdictReason: Commit 0276a66's message line 'Every element takes at least one byte on the wire' describes the floor vectorElemMinSize actually returns (it never returns less than 1, including for variable-length and degenerate nested-vector cases), so it is consistent with, not contradicted by, the recursive minimum-size logic the same commit adds.
issues.scopeReason: The commit message in question is part of this PR's own history.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Commit message allegedly contradicts the recursive minimum-size logic it introduces

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: A claim that commit 0276a66's message ("every element takes at least one byte") contradicts the recursive minimum-size logic the same commit adds was raised and judged a false positive by Codex.
